MUJAHID:v2p780/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p780/r1.speaker: كعب
MUJAHID:v2p780/r1.claim: Ka'b says humanity in loss refers to Adam and his descendants.

MUJAHID:v2p780/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p780/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p780/r2.claim: Mujahid says loss means misguidance, then the verse exempts those who believe.

MUQATIL:103:1-3/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r3.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Abū Lahab, whose name was ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.

MUQATIL:103:1-3/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r4.claim: Muqatil says Abū Lahab remains in error forever until he enters the Fire.

MUQATIL:103:1-3/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r5.claim: Those excepted—people who believe and do righteous deeds—are not in loss.

MUQATIL:103:1-3/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r7.claim: Whoever does these things belongs among the believers and righteous, escapes loss, and remains forever in the Gardens.

FARRA:v3p289/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p289/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p289/r2.claim: Khusr means punishment for sins and loss of one's family and home in Paradise.

MAJAZ:v2p310/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p310/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p310/r2.claim: Al-insān is singular in wording but collective in meaning, allowing all people to be excepted; ordinarily one would except a singular from a plural.

MAJAZ:v2p310/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p310/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p310/r3.claim: The same singular-for-collective construction occurs in Qur'an 70:19–22, where al-insān is followed by an exception for worshippers.

MAJAZ:v2p310/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p310/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p310/r4.claim: The singular wording has collective meaning; Qur'an 69:47 likewise has singular aḥad followed by plural ḥājizīn.

MAJAZ:v2p310/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p310/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p310/r5.claim: Al-Nābighah's poem illustrates generic singular wording followed by an exception.

TUSTARI:103:2/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:103:2/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:103:2/r1.claim: The person in loss is Abu Lahab, who lost all his days.

TAB-FULL:v24p517/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r1.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r1.claim: Some interpreters treat the exception as connected to the generic singular ‘human’: it has collective meaning, like ‘humanity is in loss’ in 103:2, so believers may be excepted and a superlative may be related to a plural group.

TAB-FULL:v24p520/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r5.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r5.claim: Hasan reads the exception after Hell as parallel to the exception of believers from loss in Surat al-Asr.

TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r4.claim: ‘Humanity is in loss’ means that the son of Adam is in ruin and diminishment.

TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r5.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r5.claim: Ali is reported to recite an expanded reading that calls time ‘the vicissitudes of time’ and says humanity remains in loss until the end of time.

TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r6.claim: Qatadah notes a reading that adds that humanity remains in loss until the end of time.

TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r7.claim: Mujahid explains the exception as those who believe.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says all people are in loss; belief alone is not enough, and the verse successively requires good works, mutual counsel in truth, and mutual counsel in patience.

NAHHAS:v5p286/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p286/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p286/r2.claim: Al-insān means people collectively, and loss is entry into the Fire, the greatest loss.

SULAMI:v2p419#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p419#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p419#2/r1.claim: Humanity is in loss when people neglect God's rights, follow desires, and do not fear Him.

THALABI:v10p283#3/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r12.speaker: إبراهيم
THALABI:v10p283#3/r12.claim: He says human life declines with age into weakness, except believers, whose good works from youth, strength, and health continue to be recorded.

THALABI:v10p283#3/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r13.speaker: علي
THALABI:v10p283#3/r13.claim: One reading attributed to Ali adds that a person remains in loss until the end of time.

THALABI:v10p283#3/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v10p283#3/r14.claim: The same reading is attributed to Ibn Masud, extending the state of loss to the end of time.

THALABI:v10p283#3/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r15.speaker: علي
THALABI:v10p283#3/r15.claim: Another reading attributed to Ali renders al-asr as the vicissitudes of time and adds that the person remains in loss until time’s end.

THALABI:v10p283#3/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p283#3/r16.claim: The sound reading is the one followed by the general reciters and standard codices.

THALABI:v10p283#3/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r17.speaker: أبي بن كعب
THALABI:v10p283#3/r17.claim: Ubayy says he recited the surah to the Prophet and asked him for its interpretation.

THALABI:v10p283#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p283#3/r6.claim: All people are in loss except those who believe and do righteous deeds.

THALABI:v10p284/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p284/r1.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v10p284/r1.claim: The Prophet says al-asr is an oath by God on behalf of the audience at the day’s end; he identifies the person in loss with Abu Jahl and the believers, righteous deeds, truth, and patience in turn with Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali.

THALABI:v10p284/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p284/r2.speaker: علي بن عبد الله بن عباس
THALABI:v10p284/r2.claim: While preaching from the Prophet’s pulpit, he recited the surah and repeated the same identifications of Abu Jahl, Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali with its phrases.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r10.claim: Mawardi also says loss means punishment, citing a Qur'anic phrase about the outcome of an affair.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r11.speaker: علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r11.claim: Ali is reported to read: by the era and the calamities of time, mankind is in loss throughout time.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r6.claim: Mankind here means humanity as a whole.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says it means evil.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r9.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r9.claim: Ibn Shajara says it means decrease.

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r11.claim: Human loss has two kinds: loss in deeds becomes clear in the final outcome, while loss in spiritual states becomes clear in the present moment.

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r12.claim: Loss in spiritual states appears as contraction after expansion, veiling after nearness, and returning to dispensations after choosing the harder and better path.

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r13.claim: The additional form of state loss is returning to dispensations after preferring the harder and better path.

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r7.claim: “Humanity” refers to the human species, and loss means perdition.

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r8.claim: Humanity is in punishment for its sins.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p296#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p296#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p296#2/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Zajjaj read al-insan as humankind collectively, a generic noun for all people.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p296#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p296#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p296#2/r2.claim: Al-khusr is loss or deficiency, like losing one's capital.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p296#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p296#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p296#2/r3.claim: Muqatil takes the loss as worldly misguidance: here al-insan means the unbeliever, excluded from the next verse's exception, who remains astray until death.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p296#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p296#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p296#2/r4.claim: Al-Farra says it is punishment for sins and loss of one's family, home, and property in Paradise.

WAHIDI-QT:103:2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:103:2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:103:2/r1.claim: Al-insan means the unbeliever who works outside God's obedience; he loses his family, place, and station in Paradise.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:103:1-3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:103:1-3/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:103:1-3/r2.claim: The person in loss is the disbeliever who works outside obedience and forfeits family, place, and home in Paradise.

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r10.claim: One report says the verse about humanity's loss was revealed concerning Abū Jahl.

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r12.claim: The warning and exception apply generally, as shown by the form of the exception.

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r19.claim: Humanity is in ruin because no loss exceeds deserving lasting punishment; the wording may state an inevitable outcome or loss from wasted deeds and deserved Hell.

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r20.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r20.claim: He explains loss as the nullification of deeds and deserving the Fire.

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r21.speaker: الأخفش
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r21.claim: He explains khusr as ruin or loss.

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r3.speaker: الأعرج
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r3.claim: He reads khusr with ḍamma on the sīn; the common reading has sukūn.

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r7.claim: Khusr is the loss or destruction of one's capital.

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r9.claim: The wāw in al-ʿaṣr is an oath particle; the oath's answer is “humanity is surely in loss.”

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r15.speaker: إبراهيم عن ابن عون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r15.claim: Ibrahim, transmitted by Ibn Awn, says aging and infirmity bring decline, except for believers whose youthful, healthy deeds continue to be recorded; this parallels 95:4–6.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r8.claim: Khusran means loss and diminution; one reported interpretation limits the human in loss to the unbeliever because believers are then excepted.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r9.claim: Loss is the destruction of a person's capital, the self and its lifetime, through sins; these are the person's greatest assets.

KASHSHAF:103:2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:103:2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:103:2/r1.claim: Al-insān refers to humanity as a class.

KASHSHAF:103:2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:103:2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:103:2/r2.claim: Khusr means loss, just as kufr can mean kufrān.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r6.claim: Al-insan refers to humanity as a species.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r7.claim: Khusr means loss, like the use of kufr for kufran.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#3/r2.speaker: عاصم والأعرج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#3/r2.claim: Asim and al-Aʿraj pronounce khusr with ḍamma on the sin.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#3/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#3/r5.claim: The codex of Abd Allah ibn Masud reads that God created humanity in loss.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p225/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p225/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p225/r1.claim: The statement that humankind is in loss is the answer to the oath.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p225/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p225/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p225/r2.claim: Al-insān means people collectively; khusr and khusrān have the same meaning.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p225/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p225/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p225/r3.claim: Loss means destruction or reduction of capital; a person who fails to use the self for lasting profit loses the self, their greatest capital.

RAZI:103:2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r1.claim: The definite article in الإنسان may refer to humanity as a class or to a previously known individual.

RAZI:103:2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r10.claim: The indefinite خسر may magnify the loss: it is immense beyond human comprehension because sin is against God and against great blessings.

RAZI:103:2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r11.claim: Alternatively, the indefinite may belittle the loss by implying human loss is less than Satan’s, a consoling reminder that someone is more disobedient.

RAZI:103:2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r12.claim: The author says the magnifying interpretation is the correct one.

RAZI:103:2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r13.claim: Although الإنسان is involved in many losses, the singular wording points to the true loss: deprivation of serving God; loss of Paradise and punishment are negligible by comparison.

RAZI:103:2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r14.claim: The purpose of creation is worship, so all other purposes are negligible by comparison.

RAZI:103:2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r15.claim: The emphatic إن and lām, together with في, portray a person immersed and surrounded by loss.

RAZI:103:2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r16.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r16.claim: The particle إن adds emphasis to the assertion of loss.

RAZI:103:2/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r17.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r17.claim: One construal takes في خسر as being on the path to loss, as with consuming an orphan’s wealth “in their bellies” when the outcome is Fire.

RAZI:103:2/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r18.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r18.claim: Another construal says no person escapes loss because life is capital that is continually spent.

RAZI:103:2/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r19.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r19.claim: Every hour spent in sin is loss; even permissible activity loses time without lasting effect, although it could have been used for enduring work.

RAZI:103:2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r2.claim: On the generic reading, the verse means humanity generally is in loss, as the following exception for believers indicates.

RAZI:103:2/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r20.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r20.claim: Even worship can fall short: devotion has endlessly higher degrees as knowledge of God’s majesty grows, so settling for a lower degree is a kind of loss.

RAZI:103:2/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r21.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r21.claim: Humanity tends toward loss because afterlife-directed motives are hidden while worldly motives—senses, desire, and anger—are obvious, leaving most people absorbed in the world.

RAZI:103:2/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r22.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r22.claim: The apparent contrast with Surah al-Tin is resolved by distinguishing bodily conditions there from the soul’s conditions here.

RAZI:103:2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:103:2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies a specific group of polytheists: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-As ibn Waʾil, and al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Muttalib.

RAZI:103:2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI:103:2/r4.claim: Muqatil says the verse was revealed about Abu Lahab.

RAZI:103:2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r5.speaker: خبر مرفوع
RAZI:103:2/r5.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet identifies the person as Abu Jahl; no grading is stated.

RAZI:103:2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r6.claim: A report says these people used to claim Muhammad was in loss, so God swore that the opposite was true.

RAZI:103:2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r7.claim: خسر means loss or decrease, like خسران and كفران, and can mean losing one’s capital.

RAZI:103:2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r8.claim: If الإنسان is generic, loss means wasting one’s self and lifetime, except for believers who gain everlasting bliss through them.

RAZI:103:2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r9.claim: If الإنسان means unbelievers, loss is error and disbelief, from which those who believe escape into profit.

RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r1.claim: The definite article in “al-insan” may refer either to humanity generically or to a previously understood particular person.

RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r10.claim: The indefinite “khusr” can magnify the loss or belittle it; Razi prefers magnification, a loss whose full extent only God knows because the sin is against God and His immense blessings.

RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r11.claim: On the belittling reading, human loss is less than Satan's, which offers reassurance that others are more disobedient.

RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r12.claim: Although “loss” is singular, the real loss is deprivation from serving the Lord; loss of Paradise and falling into Hell are negligible by comparison, since creation's highest purpose is worship.

RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r2.claim: The generic interpretation compares the usage to saying that dirhams have become plentiful among people; the exception of believers supports this reading.

RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse refers to a group of polytheists, including al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-As ibn Wa'il, and al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Muttalib.

RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r4.claim: Muqatil says the verse was revealed about Abu Lahab.

RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r5.claim: An unspecified raised report identifies the person as Abu Jahl.

RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r6.claim: A report says these opponents used to claim that Muhammad was in loss, so God swears the truth is the opposite of their assumption.

RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r7.claim: “Khusr” means loss or diminution, the wasting of one's capital.

RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r8.claim: If “al-insan” is generic, loss means the destruction of one's self and lifetime, except for believers, who gain everlasting happiness through them.

RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p82#2/r9.claim: If “al-insan” means a particular unbeliever, loss means misguidance and disbelief; belief turns that loss into profit.

RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r1.claim: “Lafi khusr” depicts a person immersed in loss and surrounded by it on every side.

RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r10.claim: The apparent reversal with al-Tin is resolved because that sura describes bodily states, while this one describes the soul; thus they do not contradict each other.

RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r2.claim: The particle “inna” adds emphasis to the declaration of human loss.

RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r3.claim: Razi offers two readings of the lām in “lafi”: being on the road to loss, or being continually unable to escape loss.

RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r4.claim: On the first reading, humans are on the path to loss, as those who consume orphans' wealth are said to have fire in their bellies because that is their outcome.

RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r5.claim: On the second reading, everyone incurs some loss because life's passing hours are capital that people rarely preserve.

RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r6.claim: Time spent in sin is plainly a loss.

RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r7.claim: Time spent in permissible activities is also lost because it leaves no lasting trace despite the chance to do enduring work.

RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r8.claim: Even time spent in worship is loss if one settles for a lower form, since the ranks of humility and knowledge of God's majesty have no end.

RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p83/r9.claim: Human happiness lies in loving the afterlife and turning from worldly life, but its causes are hidden while the senses, appetites, and anger draw people visibly toward this world, so most are absorbed in it and lost.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي صالح
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Abu Salih, says the human in loss is a disbeliever.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r10.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r10.claim: Ali is said to have read an explanatory addition about the calamities of time and humanity remaining in loss to the end of time.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r11.speaker: إبراهيم
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r11.claim: Ibrahim says humans decline and weaken as they age, except believers whose youthful deeds continue to earn reward, paralleling the account of human creation and decline.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r12.claim: Qurtubi calls the received community and codex reading correct and says a variant attributed to Ali is not Qur'an for recitation, referring readers to his earlier rebuttal of departures from Uthman's codex.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r2.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits Ibn Abbas's identification of the disbelievers as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-As ibn Wa'il, and the two men named al-Aswad.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r3.claim: Another interpretation reads al-insan generically as the human race.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r5.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r5.claim: Al-Farra glosses it as punishment and cites the outcome of a ruined affair.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses loss as evil; other views say deprivation, with the meanings close to one another.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r7.speaker: سلام
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r7.claim: Salam transmits a reading of al-asr with a kasra on the sad.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r8.speaker: الأعرج وطلحة وعيسى الثقفي
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r8.claim: Al-A'raj, Talha, and Isa al-Thaqafi read khusr with a damma on the sin; Harun transmits it from Abu Bakr from Asim.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:103:2/r9.claim: The vowel variants follow one another, like the variants usr and usr.

BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r2.claim: Humanity loses through its pursuits and expenditure of life; the definite noun marks the whole species and the indefinite خسر magnifies loss.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p355#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p355#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p355#7/r1.claim: The human species is in loss through its commerce.

QASHANI:103:1-3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:103:1-3/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:103:1-3/r1.claim: Affliction falls first on prophets, then saints, then the best people in descending order of spiritual excellence.

QASHANI:103:1-3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:103:1-3/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:103:1-3/r2.claim: Affliction is God’s whip, by which He drives His servants toward Himself.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وابن الزبير والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn al-Zubayr, and most authorities say the surah is Meccan; Mujāhid, Qatada, and Muqātil say Madinan.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r2.claim: After the previous warning against rivalry and repeated threat, this surah distinguishes the state of believer from unbeliever.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r2.claim: Al-ʿaṣr and al-insān are generic nouns, allowing the exception; khusr is another form of khusrān, and losing both worlds is the greatest loss.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r3.claim: Trading the afterlife for worldly life is utter loss, whereas the believer buys the afterlife with worldly life and gains; mutual counsel is to follow established truth and persevere in obedience and against sins.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r4.claim: The majority read khusr with a still sīn; Ibn Hurmuz, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and others read it with ḍamma.

SAMIN-DURR:103:2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:103:2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:103:2/r1.claim: ‘Al-insan’ is generic, with the exception that follows serving as evidence for this broad scope.

SAMIN-DURR:103:2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:103:2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:103:2/r2.claim: The common reading has a still sīn in ‘khusr’; Zayd ibn ‘Ali, Ibn Hurmuz, and one transmission from ‘Asim use ḍamma, like ‘‘usr’ and ‘yusr’.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r2.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r2.claim: A report says that before accepting Islam, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ told Musaylima that a brief, eloquent sūra had been revealed and recited al-ʿAṣr; Musaylima answered with a parody.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r3.claim: Al-Wabr is a small animal resembling a cat, notable for its ears; Musaylima's incoherent imitation failed to impress even an idol-worshipper.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r4.claim: Al-Kharāʾiṭī also recorded this story, or something close to it, in the second part of his book on bad character.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن حصن أبو مدينة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī reports that two Companions would recite Sūrat al-ʿAṣr to each other whenever they met, then exchange greetings before parting.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r6.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r6.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says that if people reflected on this sūra, it would suffice them.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r1.speaker: الشافعي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r1.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says this surah would suffice people if no other revelation had come; another reported view says it gathers all Qur'anic sciences.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r2.claim: The surah distinguishes the saved human essence from the doomed and teaches salvation by leaving the transient for the lasting; the name al-ʿAṣr signals extraction of an essence.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r4.speaker: الغزالي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r4.claim: Al-Ghazālī likens the Qur'an to a sea containing six minerals: knowledge of God, His attributes and acts, the afterlife, worship, doubts that harm faith, and lessons from the saved and ruined.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r5.claim: The surah begins with examples of the ruined and saved because preventing harm precedes securing benefit.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r6.claim: The surah's other clauses map to knowledge of God and the afterlife, required and preparatory worship, and patience that completes the effort to avoid doubt and harm.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r7.claim: The basmala says all things perish except God, whose mercy reaches everyone and whose completed gifts distinguish His chosen allies.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r1.speaker: الشافعي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r1.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says this surah would suffice people if no other revelation had come; another reported view says it gathers all Qur'anic sciences.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r2.claim: The surah distinguishes the saved human essence from the doomed and teaches salvation by leaving the transient for the lasting; the name al-ʿAṣr signals extraction of an essence.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r4.speaker: الغزالي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r4.claim: Al-Ghazālī likens the Qur'an to a sea containing six minerals: knowledge of God, His attributes and acts, the afterlife, worship, doubts that harm faith, and lessons from the saved and ruined.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r5.claim: The surah begins with examples of the ruined and saved because preventing harm precedes securing benefit.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r6.claim: The surah's other clauses map to knowledge of God and the afterlife, required and preparatory worship, and patience that completes the effort to avoid doubt and harm.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r7.claim: The basmala says all things perish except God, whose mercy reaches everyone and whose completed gifts distinguish His chosen allies.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r5.claim: Humankind is the noblest species, formed in the best proportion, just as ʿaṣr is the essence of time and pressing extracts an essence from things.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r6.claim: People generally lose by spending time on desires and present pleasures while neglecting what is lasting; unbelievers lose through denial, and sinful believers in proportion to their disobedience.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r7.claim: Even this general loss shows the need for messengers to teach which beliefs and practices please God, so obedience places people among the saved rather than the condemned.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r8.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links human loss to al-Takāthur: it narrows human understanding to immediate life and turns attention from the future where success lies.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r1.claim: Human nature is marked by deficiency, injustice, and ignorance, so people are liable to distraction by accumulation unless God grants faith.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r2.claim: The general judgment on humankind applies to all by nature, while the very few God preserves from human defects are excepted.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r3.claim: Those excepted are few relative to the people in loss; God preserves them from the inclinations and shortcomings of human nature.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r5.claim: He links this surah to earlier warnings about human ignorance and injustice and cites the ungrateful person, humanity in loss, and the man who thinks wealth makes him immortal.

DURR-FULL:v8p622/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p622/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p622/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the person in loss as Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r7.claim: Al-insan denotes the human race inclusively, as shown by the valid exception; khusr is loss of one's self and lifespan as capital, and the indefinite form magnifies a loss whose full extent only God knows.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#2/r1.claim: Humanity is in loss through its ventures, efforts, and lifetimes spent on aims that do not benefit in the afterlife and may harm them.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#2/r2.claim: The definite article in loss is comprehensive because of the exception that follows; the indefinite form either magnifies the loss or identifies a kind humans do not recognize.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r1.claim: Time gathers every kind of change, benefit, harm, and wonder; the oath draws attention to how people fare in gain or loss within it.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r10.claim: The oath warns that time consumes life and leaves people in loss unless they believe and do good works.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r11.claim: In an elegy for his teacher and the Balkan War dead, the author portrays life as deceiving people while death draws its nourishment and each breath weaves shrouds.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r12.claim: People wrongly blame time for their misfortunes; a cited poem says time is not corrupt, but people themselves are.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r13.claim: The oath honors time as a valuable blessing and says those who fail to work toward reform are themselves in loss.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r2.claim: Human life is precious capital; each unprofitable instant wastes it, but a final righteous act may make up for years of waste and win eternal paradise.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r3.claim: Sufis say a person should be the child of the moment: value the present and use it to gain good for the afterlife.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r4.claim: People who deny the afterlife also urge seizing the present for worldly pleasure, though their aim differs from the Sufi's afterlife-oriented use of time.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r5.claim: Time is the opportunity for action, whether productive or wasteful, profitable or harmful; the oath highlights the value and nature of life's moments.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r6.claim: Time's senses of restraint and bestowal can support both the loss side and the exception of those who gain through faith and good works.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r7.claim: A cited couplet says each passing day takes away part of the speaker, since nothing is more precious than life.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r8.claim: People fail to calculate what they gained against the life they spent and wrongly imagine that passing time means they are growing.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r9.claim: A poem says people rejoice at days passing although each one reduces their remaining lifespan.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r1.claim: The first Prophetic-era phase began with Muhammad's mission amid religious disorder, extinguished guidance, and widespread ignorance, disbelief, injustice, and corruption.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r2.claim: The Qur'an began descending with the command iqra on a Night of Power, and prophetic light rose to call humanity toward reform, paradise, and divine approval.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r3.claim: As discussed in Surat al-Bayyina, spreading the upright religion called people away from total loss and began transformations that led from the middle ages to the last era.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r4.claim: The oath by this era before the declaration that humanity is in loss except believers and doers of good carries important meaning.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r10.claim: The generic al-insan, signaled by the following exception, means all humanity across eras, especially people of the last era, are in absolute loss except those named next.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r11.claim: Husr means losing rather than gaining, wasting capital, and ending in bankruptcy, sorrow, and deprivation; the indefinite form magnifies or specifies the kind of loss.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r12.claim: Life is humanity's capital: it is spent with every breath and hour, while accountability for this blessing approaches.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r13.claim: Life is a limited loan belonging to the Creator, entrusted to people to invest well; their benefit depends on the profit made by spending it.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r14.claim: A person receives only what they strive for and is held accountable for what they earn.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r15.claim: After returning the loaned capital to its owner, people are saved and rewarded according to their profit or left liable, bankrupt, and punished according to their deficit; the scales express this reckoning.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r16.claim: Every breath spent idly is loss; a worldly or neutral act leaves no lasting gain, evil is certainly loss, and even obedience could have been done better.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r17.claim: Because knowledge of Allah and His majesty can grow without limit, greater knowledge should produce deeper awe and love and more complete worship; settling for less entails some loss.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r18.claim: Obstacles and constricting events that assail people compound the danger and loss inherent in the passing of time.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r19.claim: Even if people enjoyed constant comfort, their lives move toward death and each passing breath is itself a death.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r20.speaker: Râzî
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r20.claim: Razi says loss is humanity's basic condition: true happiness is loving the afterlife rather than attaching oneself to worldly pain and pleasure, yet most people pursue the world and are ruined.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r21.claim: Those with the four traits named in the next verse are exceptions to loss and instead gain.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r9.claim: The oath encompasses every meaning of asr, especially the final era as the afternoon of time and the age of Muhammad, before the declaration that humankind is in loss.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r10.claim: True faith in the real and abiding God cannot fail; a life spent in beautiful works for God is never wasted, while faith in falsehood and its deeds vanish.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r11.claim: The verse implies that even people with true faith incur a kind of loss if they do not perform righteous deeds and counsel truth and patience.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r12.speaker: Mürcienin
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r12.claim: The Murji'a claim that lack of action causes no loss once faith exists is false; Ahl al-Sunna correctly holds that sinful, disobedient believers also incur a kind of loss.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r13.claim: Although faith ultimately saves sinful believers, those whose sins outweigh their good deeds undergo Hell's loss until their sins are cleansed.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r14.speaker: Ebû Medîne
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r14.claim: He reports that two of the Prophet's Companions would not part after meeting until they recited Sūrat al-ʿAṣr to each other and then exchanged greetings.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r9.claim: Only those with faith, righteous works, mutual counsel in truth, and mutual counsel in patience are exceptions to humanity's otherwise absolute loss; all four express complete faith.

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r1.claim: The rendering says: By the age; humankind is in absolute loss, except those who believe, do righteous works, counsel one another to truth, and counsel patience.

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r13.claim: Afternoon evokes humanity's creation late in the world's day, the closing period of human life, and the sorrow of returning without gain; this complements the previous surah's warning about rivalry.

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r15.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits Ali's interpretive recitation: by time and its calamities, humankind remains in loss until time's end.

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r16.claim: This reading interprets asr as dehr, whose recurring calamities and changes warn people and whose loss continues to the end; squeezing or confinement may also reinforce the loss side.

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r17.claim: Another view says dehr contains every wonder that displays the Creator's power, where ordinary and extraordinary events, blessings, disasters, gains, and losses unfold.

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan, has three verses, and compresses Islam's full way of life and the Muslim community's identity and role into a brief constitution.

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r2.claim: The surah presents the Muslim community's essence and function in its final verse, a concise form of inimitable divine expression.

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r3.claim: Across all ages there is one successful path: faith, righteous action, and mutual exhortation to truth and patience; every other way ends in loss.

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r30.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r30.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r30.claim: Qutb sees worldly loss spreading because humanity turns away from God's good and lacks righteous authority; he says Muslims who claim Islam have strayed furthest from its guidance.

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r44.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r44.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r44.claim: Earthly profit and loss are small beside the lasting stakes of Paradise and God's pleasure; the final loss is the collapse of human dignity.

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r45.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r45.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r45.claim: The surah decisively sets one route out of loss: faith, righteous work, and a community that mutually guards truth with patience.

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r46.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r46.speaker: الرجلان من أصحاب رسول الله
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r46.claim: Qutb reports that two Companions would not part after meeting until one recited Surat al-Asr to the other, renewing their commitment to its guidance.

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r1.claim: Qutb treats mutual exhortation to truth and patience as defining the Muslim community's distinct identity and bond.

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r2.claim: Across all ages there is one successful path: faith, righteous action, and mutual exhortation to truth and patience; every other way ends in loss.

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r29.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r29.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r29.claim: Qutb sees worldly loss spreading because humanity turns away from God's good and lacks righteous authority; he says Muslims who claim Islam have strayed furthest from its guidance.

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r43.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r43.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r43.claim: Earthly profit and loss are small beside the lasting stakes of Paradise and God's pleasure; the final loss is the collapse of human dignity.

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r44.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r44.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r44.claim: The surah decisively sets one route out of loss: faith, righteous work, and a community that mutually guards truth with patience.

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r45.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r45.speaker: الرجلان من أصحاب رسول الله
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r45.claim: Qutb reports that two Companions would not part after meeting until one recited Surat al-Asr to the other, renewing their commitment to its guidance.

IBNASHUR:103:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:2/r1.claim: Al-insan is a generic definite with customary comprehensive force: people living when Islam appeared, especially those reached by its call across the world; after the exception of believers who do good, the judgment remains true of others.

IBNASHUR:103:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:2/r2.claim: Loss, the opposite of profit in trade, is a metaphor for the bad afterlife outcome of someone who expects a good end, whether bliss or punishment; it echoes the cited verse about an unprofitable trade.

IBNASHUR:103:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:2/r3.claim: The phrase in loss uses figurative containment: being enclosed by loss is stronger than simply calling a person a loser.

IBNASHUR:103:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:2/r4.claim: The universal assertion, strengthened by the oath and emphatic particle, warns of the condition enveloping most people.

TABATABAI:103:1-3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r1.claim: The surah condenses Quranic teachings and gathers its aims in the briefest statement; although it could be Meccan or Medinan, it seems more likely Meccan.

TABATABAI:103:1-3/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r10.claim: The indefinite khusr either magnifies the loss or denotes a distinct kind, beyond financial and status losses; the Quran calls loss of self and family at Judgment manifest loss.

TABATABAI:103:1-3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r8.claim: Al-insan means humankind generally; khusr is loss of capital, whether attributed to a person or to an action such as trade.

TABATABAI:103:1-3/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r9.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r9.claim: Raghib notes that loss is attributed either to a person, as in someone losing, or to an action, as in a trade losing.

TABATABAI:103:2-3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:2-3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:103:2-3/r1.claim: Earthly life is a test that determines the felicity or misery of the enduring afterlife.

TABATABAI:103:2-3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:2-3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:103:2-3/r2.claim: Belief and righteous action bring afterlife happiness, whereas disbelief and sin bring misery; life's capital is spent through belief and action, yielding profit by following truth or loss by following falsehood.

ASAD-NOTES:103:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:103:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:103:intro/r1.claim: The surah was revealed shortly after surah 94, Ash-Sharh.

BINTSHATI:v2p80/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p80/r5.speaker: المفسرون
BINTSHATI:v2p80/r5.claim: Exegetes differ between taking the human as all people and as particular Meccan opponents; reports name al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-As ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Lahab, or Abu Jahl.

BINTSHATI:v2p81/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p81/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p81/r1.claim: The author notes that the exception of believers would break if humanity meant only the named Meccan opponents.

BINTSHATI:v2p81/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p81/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p81/r4.claim: The Quran's use of al-nas denotes humanity broadly, while al-ins appears in contexts paired with jinn and carries the sense of human beings as the opposite of wild creatures.

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r1.claim: The three-rhyme sura is an opening single-member oath by late afternoon, followed by a rebuke; verse 3 exempts believers and differentiates good from bad people.

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r3.claim: The commentator finds no hymn-like resonance in this sura and points to a critical discussion of Neuwirth's hypothesis elsewhere.

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r4.speaker: Robinson
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r4.claim: Robinson's secular reading makes ʿaṣr the time when merchants count a day's earnings, linking the oath's image of profit to the eschatological loss in verse 2.

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r5.claim: Robinson's reading is strengthened by Q 104, which also contrasts worldly wealth with damnation in the hereafter.

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r6.speaker: Spitaler
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r6.claim: Medina II joins the oath verse to verse 2 in its verse division.

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r1.speaker: Zirker
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r1.claim: The German translation of the verse follows Zirker.

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r2.claim: The verse may mean that human conduct causes people to forfeit bliss in the hereafter.

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Torrey
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r3.claim: Torrey compares this eschatological loss with Luke 9:24; the Syriac Peshitta uses ḥsar, from the same root as Arabic ḫasira and ḫusr.

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r4.claim: Philippians 3:7–8 offers another comparison for the notion of loss.

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r5.speaker: Torrey
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r5.claim: Torrey documents many other Qur'anic examples of ḫasira and ḫusr used eschatologically.

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:2:anmerkung/r6.claim: An early Meccan parallel is the phrase ḫāsirah in Q 79:12.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r1.claim: Al-ʿAṣr follows al-Takāthur’s warning against wasting life amassing wealth; people would have used life wisely if they knew they must answer for this great blessing.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r2.claim: This sūrah explains life’s real value and the factors that make it a path to salvation or a cause of eternal punishment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r2.claim: The sūrah briefly lays out the way to use life well and thereby fulfill the individual and collective duties on which salvation depends.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r3.claim: The Qur’an’s guidance to organize personal and collective life for success in the Hereafter is condensed into these three verses.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r4.speaker: Im ām Sh āfi‘ ī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r4.claim: Imām Shāfiʿī is reported to say that reflective reading of Sūrah al-ʿAṣr alone would suffice for people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r4.claim: The lifespan is valuable yet rapidly consumed, so everyone is losing except those who believe and do good deeds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r1.claim: Faith and righteous action fulfill life’s purpose: defying Satan brings mutual pleasure with God and Paradise, while surrendering to Satan’s lures forfeits an extraordinary favor.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r2.speaker: Im ām Far āhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r2.claim: Farāhī traces īmān to amn, with senses of giving peace, attesting or trusting, and having absolute faith; muʾmin is also a divine name because God grants safety to those who seek refuge.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r3.speaker: Im ām Far āhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r3.claim: Farāhī defines religious īmān as certainty joined with humility, trust, and adherence: a believer accepts God’s signs and commands, submits to Him, and accepts His decisions.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r4.claim: Righteous deeds follow as faith’s necessary corollary: true faith should shape actions, and their absence shows that faith has not taken firm root.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p439/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p439/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p439/r1.claim: Islahi explains that inward faith can be self-deception, so words alone do not prove belief; a person’s deeds must also testify to faith.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p439/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p439/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p439/r2.claim: The Qur’anic address to those who believe with the tongue calls them to believe through their deeds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p439/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p439/r3.speaker: Im ām Far āhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p439/r3.claim: Farāhī explains ṣāliḥāt as actions that enable apparent and inward, worldly and religious, individual and collective development toward human potential.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p440/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p440/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p440/r1.claim: Righteous deeds accord with God’s wise design for the universe’s collective order, since the world is governed by purposeful prudence rather than play.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r4.claim: Faith is presented as the foundation and nucleus, with righteous deeds following as its explanation.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r17.claim: Despite its brevity, Surah al-Asr contains a rich summary of the Qur'an's religious and moral duties and counsels.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r18.speaker: İmam Şâfiî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r18.claim: Al-Shafi'i is quoted as saying that this short surah alone would suffice humanity if nothing else had been revealed, since it embraces all Qur'anic sciences.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r19.speaker: Mehmet Âkif Ersoy
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r19.claim: Akif's poem presents true faith, righteous conduct, truth, and steadfastness as the sequence that saves humanity from loss.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r6.claim: God swears by this precious reality to stress time's value and warn that a person who fails to use it well ends in loss.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r7.claim: Here, loss means the punishment of the hereafter, the greatest loss for someone who has wasted life and time, as Ibn Ashur is cited.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r16.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r16.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r16.claim: The exception here requires faith and good works, whereas al-ʿAṣr adds mutual exhortation to truth and patience; that added practice prevents further loss of reward.

STUDYQURAN:103:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r4.claim: This reading applies to individuals and humanity's history: each generation falls a degree below the previous one.

STUDYQURAN:103:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:2/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:2/r1.claim: Verses 2–3 answer the oath and parallel 95:5–6.

STUDYQURAN:103:2/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:2/r2.speaker: Bg and Q
STUDYQURAN:103:2/r2.claim: Mankind can mean disbelievers; another reading takes it as humanity generally.

STUDYQURAN:103:2/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:2/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:2/r3.claim: In light of the declining day, mankind can refer to humanity in the final phase of the historical cycle.

STUDYQURAN:103:2/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:2/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:2/r4.claim: Disbelief increases disbelievers only in loss; Qur'anic loss encompasses both this world and the Hereafter.

STUDYQURAN:103:2/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:2/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:2/r5.claim: Losers lose what they value most in this life, not necessarily material goods, and later lose their souls and families at Resurrection.

STUDYQURAN:103:2/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:2/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:2/r6.claim: Spiritually, loss can mean losing faith and attachment to God; if ʿaṣr means time, misuse of time leaves people constantly losing.

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r1.claim: Al-ʿAṣr is Makkan and likely follows Sūrah 94; ʿaṣr can mean late afternoon, its last hour, afternoon, the afternoon prayer, or an epoch.

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r2.claim: Companions reportedly did not part after meeting until one recited the whole sūrah and greeted the other with peace.

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3.claim: Read after Sūrah 102, ʿaṣr can mean time generally: vying for increase wastes it, and time's blessing is what people will be questioned about.

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r4.claim: These three short verses can be seen as the whole Qur'an's message: humanity loses unless it turns to God.

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r5.speaker: al-Shāfiʿī
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r5.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī is reported to have said that if people pondered this sūrah, it would suffice them.
